page: Amazon Web Services m6g.medium is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture using Neoverse-N1 cores, it operates via the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is configured with 1 dedicated physical core mapped to 1 vCPU operating at 2.5 GHz, eliminating thread contention from simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by 4.0 GB of system memory to maintain a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local NVMe storage is not included, and the instance does not feature discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a profile governed by its single-core configuration. In single-threaded compute, the instance achieves an average score of 1499.79 on stress-ng, while its multi-core stress-ng result matches the single-core output due to the core count. Geekbench scores reach 904.0 for single-core and 891.0 for multi-core. In memory bandwidth testing, it records 59.31 GB/s for cached 16 KB read blocks, 19.48 GB/s for uncached 256 MB reads, and 9.61 GB/s for large block writes. Application-level performance includes 1.18 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 1.14 GB/s throughput for static web serving.

The instance provides cost efficiency for low-footprint deployments requiring dedicated rather than burstable or shared CPU allocation. Tradeoffs center on the absence of bundled local storage, minimal baseline networking throughput, and limited overall multi-threaded throughput. Workload fit includes microservices, lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, small Redis caching tiers, and staging or development environments operating on ARM64.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.medium is a general-purpose, single-core cloud instance based on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 Graviton processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Managed via the Nitro hypervisor, the instance pairs 1 dedicated vCPU with 4.0 GB of system memory, matching standard 1:4 general-purpose resource ratios. It features no integrated local storage and no GPU acceleration, depending entirely on network-attached volumes for block storage. In synthetic performance benchmarks, the single-core stress-ng score of 1499.79 reflects average single-thread compute density, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory write bandwidth remain limited by the single-core topology. The instance achieves 1.18 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 1.14 GB/s in static web serving tests. The m6g.medium represents a cost-effective, dedicated-core footprint suited for microservices, low-volume web servers, staging environments, and lightweight containerized services that do not demand extensive parallelism or heavy local disk operations.
